To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the mean age of breast cancer onset in LFS families was significantly lower in families with a TP53 germ-line mutation than in families without a TP53 germ line mutation.
the TP53 gene plays an important role in the pathogenesis of cancer and that the genotype-phenotype correlations that we have observed are important for the clinical management of LFS families.

(a) the TP53 mutation status in LFS families is associated with the age of breast cancer onset, (b) the genotype-phenotype relationship observed in individuals with a TP533 mutation is consistent with a functional model, and (c) the genotype- phenotype relationship in LFS/LF1 individuals is associated with a null phenotype.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of cancer predisposition syndromes and the identification of genetic markers associated with the risk of developing specific types of tumors.
the study of the genetic basis and the clinical consequences of the Li-Fraumenie syndromes.
the study of the TP53 gene as a marker of predisposition to cancer, the identification of TP53 mutations in human cancer, and the study of the biological consequences of these mutations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
TP53 germ-line mutations predisposing to cancer are heterogeneous and are associated with a variety of phenotypic manifestations.
the Li-Fraumenii syndrome is not caused by TP53 mutations but that it is associated with TP53 mutations.

LFS is a genetically heterogeneous disorder, with at least 4 different genetic mechanisms (germ-line mutations in the TP53 and MDM2 genes and loss of heterozygosity on chromosomes 17p or 9p), and that the phenotype-genotype correlations are not yet fully elucidated.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the Li-Fraumenie syndrome is a cancer predisposition syndrome with a high risk of developing a variety of cancers, especially soft tissue and bone sarcomas, breast cancer, adrenocortical carcinomas, brain tumors, and acute leukemia.
the TP53 mutation is associated with an increased risk of developing a variety of cancers, but the risk varies with the type of TP53 mutation and the type of tumor.
the Li-Fraumenii syndrome is a genetic disease caused by mutations in the TP53 tumor suppressor gene.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the genetic testing and the tumor surveillance should be done in all the members of the family, regardless the presence of the tumor.
TP53 mutations in LFS/LFS families are associated with specific clinical manifestations, and this association may be used to guide genetic testing and clinical management of these individuals.
the TP53 genotype is associated with a specific phenotype, including tumor type and age of onset.
